dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of Industrial Finance Corporation (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 1993
Purpose:
•	Transfer and Vesting: Transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India to a company formed under the Companies Act, 1956.
•	Repeal: Repeal of the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948.
Key Provisions:
1.	Transfer of Undertaking: - Vesting Entity: The undertaking vests in "The Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited" (the Company).
•	Effective Date: On the "appointed day", notified by the Central Government.
2.	Effects of Vesting: - Comprehensive Transfer: Includes all assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations.
•	Contractual Continuity: Contracts, deeds, etc., become enforceable against the Company.
•	Ongoing Proceedings: Can be continued against the Company.
3.	Concessions, Licences, and Benefits:
•	Deemed Grant: All concessions, licences, and benefits granted to the Corporation are deemed granted to the Company.
4.	Tax Implications: - Continuity of Tax Benefits: Tax exemptions, assessments, and benefits continue for the Company.
•	Capital Gains Exemption: Transfer not construed as a transfer for capital gains under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
5.	Employee Provisions: - Employment Continuity: Officers and employees (except top management) transfer with the same terms.
•	Option to Opt Out: Within six months, with no compensation for transfer.
•	Retiree Benefits: Continue from the Company.
6.	Governance and Securities: - Bankers' Books Evidence Act: The Company is deemed a bank under this Act.
•	Approved Securities: Shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company are deemed approved.
7.	Repeal and Saving Clause: - Repealed Act: Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, repealed on the appointed day.
•	Continuity of Actions: Actions under the repealed Act are deemed taken under this Act.
Important Dates:
•	Commencement: Deemed effective from 1st October 1992.
•	Repeal Effective Date: On the appointed day.

dc.identifier.next_section.value: 187.When acceptance of benefit given by will constitutes election to take under will.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
Notwithstanding anything contained in sections 180 to 185, where a particular gift is expressed in the will to be in lieu of something belonging to the legatee, which is also in terms disposed of by the will, then, if the legatee claims that thing, he must relinquish the particular gift, but he is not bound to relinquish any other benefit given to him by the will.
Illustration
Under A's marriage-settlement his wife is entitled, if she survives him, to the enjoyment of the estate of Sultanpur during her life. A by his will bequeaths to his wife an annuity of 200 rupees during her life, in lieu of her interest in the estate of Sultanpur, which estate he bequeaths to his son. He also gives his wife a legacy of 1,000 rupees. The widow elects to take what she is entitled to under the settlement. She is bound to relinquish the annuity but not the legacy of 1,000 rupees.

indexableObject.name: The Khaddar (Protection of Name) Act, 1950

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Khaddar (Protection of Name) Act, 1950

The Khaddar (Protection of Name) Act, 1950 was enacted to protect the use of the word "Khaddar" (also known as Khadi) and to prevent its misuse in trade and commerce. The Act aims to ensure that only genuine hand-spun and hand-woven cloth is marketed or sold as "Khaddar."

Key Provisions

•	The Act regulates the use of the word "Khaddar" in relation to cloth and textile products. 
•	It prohibits any person from selling, offering for sale, or advertising cloth as "Khaddar" unless it satisfies the prescribed standards. 
•	It empowers the competent authority to take action against unauthorized or fraudulent use of the name. 
•	Violations of the Act may attract penalties as prescribed. 

Importance

•	Protects the authenticity and goodwill associated with Khaddar. 
•	Supports rural artisans and the handloom sector. 
•	Promotes fair trade practices by preventing false representations. 
•	Helps maintain consumer confidence in genuine Khaddar products. 

Historical Significance

Khaddar played a vital role in India's freedom movement as a symbol of self-reliance (Swadeshi) and economic independence. The Act was introduced after Independence to preserve this heritage and prevent commercial misuse of the name.

•	Status: Repealed; protection is now provided through subsequent laws and institutional mechanisms.
